content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Using Compustat annual data, compute the year-over-year growth rate of inventories (item INVT) minus the year-over-year growth rate of sales (item SALE). Form the measure at fiscal year end and hold from June of year t+1. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals overproduction and weak future demand, leading to markdowns and disappointing earnings that the market underappreciates.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Intensity", "construction": "From Compustat, take order backlog (item OB) scaled by total assets (item AT) at fiscal year end. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "A large order backlog relative to assets reflects strong committed future demand that is not yet capitalized in current earnings, so backlog-rich firms are undervalued.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Selling Expense Efficiency Shift", "construction": "Compute the change in selling, general and administrative expense (item XSGA) divided by sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year. Measure = SGA/Sales(t) - SGA/Sales(t-1). Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "A rising SG&A-to-sales ratio signals deteriorating operating discipline and margin pressure that predicts lower future profitability and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining SG&A intensity)"}, {"name": "Trading Volume Acceleration", "construction": "Using CRSP daily data, compute average daily dollar volume over the most recent month divided by average daily dollar volume over the prior 11 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month-end.", "rationale": "A sharp acceleration in trading activity reflects heightened investor attention and speculative interest that tends to reverse, producing lower subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (decelerating volume)"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Return Skewness", "construction": "Regress daily stock excess returns on the market excess return over the trailing 12 months using CRSP data; compute the skewness of the daily residuals. Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Investors overpay for lottery-like stocks with positive idiosyncratic skewness, leading such stocks to earn lower average returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (negative idiosyncratic skewness)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Persistence", "construction": "From Compustat, compute the ratio of current capital expenditure (item CAPX) to the three-year trailing average of capital expenditure, all scaled by lagged total assets. Measure captures a spike above the firm's own investment norm. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Investment spikes above a firm's historical norm reflect managerial overextrapolation of demand and empire building, which the market overvalues and subsequently corrects.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (investment below own trend)"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Momentum", "construction": "Compute gross profit (item SALE minus item COGS) divided by sales for the current and prior fiscal year; the measure is the year-over-year change in gross margin. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Improving gross margins reflect strengthening pricing power and cost control that persist and are only slowly incorporated into prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving gross margin)"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Surprise Drift", "construction": "Using CRSP distribution codes and Compustat, flag firms that pay a cash dividend in the current fiscal year but paid none in the prior three years. Assign an indicator and hold long positions for 12 months after the announcement.", "rationale": "Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows, and the market underreacts to this signal, producing a post-initiation drift.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (recent dividend initiators)"}, {"name": "Accrual Volatility", "construction": "Compute total accruals (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding debt, minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets for each of the past five fiscal years; the measure is the standard deviation of these annual accruals. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "High volatility of accruals indicates low earnings quality and greater information risk, so investors demand higher returns to hold such stocks.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Relative Bid-Ask Spread Trend", "construction": "Using CRSP daily closing bid and ask (or NASDAQ quotes), compute the average relative quoted spread ((ask-bid)/midpoint) over the recent quarter minus that over the prior year. Measure is the change in liquidity. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Stocks whose spreads are narrowing are experiencing improving liquidity, and the liquidity premium declines gradually, so worsening-liquidity stocks require compensation via higher future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (widening spreads)"}]}
